stories.title: US, Canada fail to reach trade pact to avert new tariffs
stories.summary: The United States and Canada have failed to reach a trade deal, and the US said it would impose 50% tariffs on some imports from Canada, an escalation of tensions between the two long-time allies. A senior administration official said Section 338 tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods would go into effect just after midnight on Saturday (5am Irish time). Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said he had suspended trade negotiations and Canada would retaliate ‌dollar for dollar on ⁠the new tariffs. The decision by the US administration followed three days of talks in Washington between Canada's minister for trade with the US, Dominic LeBlanc, and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

stories.title: Irish excise on alcohol second highest in Europe - study
stories.summary: Irish consumers pay the second highest excise duty on alcohol in Europe, according to new research. The research from Dublin City University economist Anthony Foley, commissioned by the Drinks Industry Group of Ireland (DIGI), shows that Ireland comes only behind Finland when it comes to excise levies on alcohol. When broken down by type of alcoholic drink, excise on wine in Ireland is the second highest in the EU and UK, also behind Finland, while excise on beer and spirits is the third highest, behind Finland and Sweden. A pint of beer purchased in a pub here attracts an excise duty of €0.55 compared to just €0.05 in Spain and Germany.

stories.title: Dáil recall over fuel interventions under review - Burke
stories.summary: An early recall of the Dáil is "under review" by the Government leaders, a Cabinet minister has said, as measures designed to keep fuel costs down are due to be withdrawn. An excise cut of 32c on a litre of diesel and 27c for petrol is due to be phased out from September. The cuts were introduced in April amid major protests that strangled fuel distribution around the country. Today, Minister for Enterprise Peter Burke did not rule out an early return of the Dáil, which is scheduled to resume on 16 September.

stories.title: Wholesale electricity prices up 56% in 12 months to July
stories.summary: New figures from the Central Statistics Office show that wholesale electricity prices rose by 14.8% in July when compared with June and were 56.2% higher than July of last year. While wholesale electricity prices remain 59.9% lower when compared with their peak in August 2022, they reached their highest level since January 2025 last month. The CSO said that all Energy Fuels were up by 0.6% in the month and were up 19.1% since July of last year. Commenting on today's CSO figures, price comparison website Bonkers.ie said that looking at the past six months, which gives a better indication of underlying trends, wholesale electricity prices were almost 30% higher than in the previous six-month period.

stories.title: Iran vows 'devastating' response to US economic threats
stories.summary: Iran has said that its response to any new US threats would be "devastating" after Washington pledged to impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling the Iranian leadership. US Treasury chief Scott Bessent said he would give details on Monday of the planned sanctions, which follow a warning from President Donald Trump of economic consequences against any country that provided "any type of lifeline to Iran". The chief of staff of Iran's Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said the Islamic Republic's reaction would be broad and decisive. "With preparedness across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, Iran's armed forces will respond to the enemy's new threats with crushing, punishing and devastating responses," Mr Abdollahi was quoted as saying by Iranian media.

stories.title: McCartan: Newbies brought 'freshness' to Cork panel
stories.summary: After being in the last six All-Ireland camogie finals and winning three of those, it may have been difficult to change a winning formula. Getting to so many successive finals prove that Cork camogie has clearly been in a golden age. But this season saw a lot of change in the Cork camp. After a very difficult start, forward Sorcha McCartan credited a "freshness" that the new players brought into the senior camogie set up during the season just gone. "I think they brought a bit of a freshness in terms of maybe there was less of a tense atmosphere. Not that the girls that left were tense, but I suppose they were around for so long that they brought a bit of seriousness to it. "They understood the magnitude of trouble that we were in. We had one win on the board at the end of May. That's really unheard of for a Cork camogie team.

stories.title: Showgrounds showdown vital but coming years are critical
stories.summary: Friday night at the Showgrounds carries the feel of a season-defining game even with nine league matches still to play. Sligo Rovers sit bottom of the league table on 22 points, while Waterford on 28 points sit eighth - just marginally ahead of Drogheda United on goal difference. A home victory would narrow the gap to within three points and breathe life into this survival fight. A defeat creates a nine-point gap between the teams and leaves Darren Purse's side needing something close to a miracle. Both clubs enjoyed welcome FAI Cup victories last weekend. Sligo beat Kerry 4-0 while Waterford edged past Athlone Town, but the league table is where the pressure lives.

stories.title: Something for the Weekend: The Jimmy Cake's cultural picks
stories.summary: To celebrate the 25th anniversary of their seminal debut album, Brains, The Jimmy Cake will play the album in full - in their first concert in just under a decade at the National Concert Hall this November. The band formed in Dublin in the late 1990s and Brains announced their arrival proper. As a nine-piece blending accordion, clarinet, saxophone, glockenspiel, trumpet and DIY percussion around the core of guitars, bass and drums they went on to release lauded efforts such as 2002’s Dublin Gone. Everybody Dead and 2008’s Spectre and Crown before later albums Master (2015) and Tough Love (2017). Parallel to his involvement with The Jimmy Cake, pianist, synthesist, graphic designer and label manager Paul G Smyth has also set himself apart as a singular voice in Europe’s vigorous improvised music scene, working with luminaries such as Derek Bailey, Evan Parker, Peter Brötzmann and Keiji Haino. I’m being quietly haunted by a film from 2019 called I’m No Longer Here. Written and directed by Fernando Frías de la Parra, it follows an exiled Mexican teenager obsessed with slowed-down cumbia music struggling to adapt in New York after fleeing cartel violence. There’s something unspoken in it that has held me since and I don’t know what it is. "I think I know what it is," my wife said recently as she left the room. That’s helpful, isn’t it?

stories.title: Call for technology to prevent Luas dragging passengers
stories.summary: Railway accident investigators have called for all Luas trams to be fitted with new anti-drag technology after a series of incidents where passengers were dragged along station platforms after they, or their belongings, were caught in doors. A safety advice notice has been issued by the Railway Accident Investigation Unit after four separate "trap-and-drag" incidents between April and June this year. The RAIU said there was a risk of injuries or fatalities to passengers from being dragged along with a tram. In one incident at the Stillorgan stop on the Luas Green Line on 15 May, a teenage girl sustained a deep laceration to her face and grazing to her knees and hands after her coat became trapped as the doors closed before she boarded the tram.

stories.title: Building of over 3,000 homes commenced in July
stories.summary: The building of 3,028 new homes was commenced in July - an increase of 169% on the same month last year (1,125) - according to figures to be published later today by the Department of Housing. Of the new commencements last month, over half (1,612) are houses being built as part of multi-unit developments, 1,004 are apartments, with the remaining 412 made up of one-off houses. The department said that since the beginning of 2026, 18,974 new homes have been commenced, which is up 152% from the 7,539 homes commenced in the first seven months of last year. The data show it is also the second highest number of new-home commencements for the period, since recording began in 2014.

stories.title: UK retail sales soften in July after June World Cup boost
stories.summary: British retail sales fell back as expected in July after a surge in June when hot weather boosted demand for fans and air conditioners and supermarkets offered promotions alongside the men's soccer World Cup, official figures showed today. UK retail sales volumes last month dropped 0.5% from June, in line with economists' median forecast in a Reuters poll. Annual sales growth slowed to 1.6% in July from a downwardly revised 3.8%, slightly below expectations for a fall to 2.2%. The biggest drag came from clothing and footwear sales, which fell by the most since May 2025, down 2.7% on the month, after many stores began summer sales in June rather than July.

stories.summary: The world's oldest person has celebrated her 117th birthday in the UK today, attributing her longevity to moderation. Ethel Caterham has become the first person in recorded history to reach the age of 117 and is one of only 13 people in recorded history to reach the milestone. Ms Caterham, who is living in a care home in Surrey, said she "enjoyed everything in life but in moderation". "I never argue with anyone. But Arsenal’s one-sided opening-night win cements their status as the bookmakers’ pre-season favourites. Arsenal’s home matches last season were riddled with anxiety as the Gunners attempted to end a grisly streak of near-misses and land their first title in two decades.

stories.title: Kobe-mania and the Irish experiment
stories.summary: The AFL's Irish experiment nearly failed before even it really even began - and it all came down to a split-second decision in the 1987 Victorian Football League preliminary final between Melbourne and Hawthorn. The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. Kept alive by Melbourne’s inefficiency, Gary Buckenara was given one last chance to win it from Hawthorn but from way out, it was a low percentage chance.

stories.summary: There will be more than 300 free events taking place across Dublin city next month as part of the capital's Culture Night. For the first time, performances will extend onto North Earl Street, with a series of events and an open-air concert. Across the city, people can expect everything from tango and trad music to painting, poetry, and pole dancing. Also museums, galleries, heritage sites, artists' studios, and independent venues will open their doors to the public, after hours, for the night.

stories.title: Noah Kahan to play Aviva Stadium next year
stories.summary: American singer Noah Kahan will play his biggest ever Irish show when he performs at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on 17th of July 2027 as part of his The Last Of The Bugs Tour. The Stick Season star also plays three previously announced and now sold-out shows in the 3Arena this November, along with his biggest ever headline show when he plays Wembley Stadium in London next July. The two-time Grammy nominated Vermont singer scored a huge breakout hit with his song and album Stick Season in 2022 and released his fourth album The Great Divide earlier this year, alongside Kahan's Netflix documentary, Noah Kahan: Out of Body. He played his biggest Irish headline show to date in Dublin's Marlay Park last summer in front of a crowd of 39,000. He also played Electric Picnic in 2024.

stories.title: The fascinating history behind the 'clean girl aesthetic'
stories.summary: Laura Fitzachary is a historian and historical content creator based in Dublin who specialises in fashion and beauty history in Ireland and beyond. Fashion and beauty historian Laura Fitzachary writes about sounding the death knell for 'clean girl' beauty, and what its life cycle as a trend tells us about makeup history. With a focus on health, natural beauty and minimalism (albeit through the skewed lens of Western beauty standards...), the 'clean girl aesthetic' appeared in 2020, becoming a lifestyle trend enthusiastically endorsed and proliferated on social media, particularly TikTok. You'll no doubt have seen versions of it: the dewy skin, the glossy blush, the barely there mascara and impeccably groomed brows, all topped off with a shiny slicked-back bun.

stories.title: Hundreds attend vigil held for family injured in M9 crash
stories.summary: Hundreds of people have attended a prayer vigil for four members of a family injured in last weekend's crash on the M9 in Co Kildare. The vigil was held in St Clare's Church in Graiguecullen, Co Carlow. The church was full and some people had to be accommodated in the nearby parish centre, where the vigil was being live-streamed. Three women and a seven-year-old boy were travelling to Dublin Airport when their car collided with a car being driven in the wrong direction down the motorway. They remain in hospital, where they are being treated for serious injuries.

stories.title: 79% of adults interested in new savings scheme - research
stories.summary: The vast majority of adults in Ireland (79%) are interested in investing in the Government's new planned Savings and Investment Account, research from the Banking & Payments Federation Ireland (BPFI) suggests. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris is expected to announce details of the State-backed scheme in October's Budget, which is due to be up and running next year. It will likely include a single flat rate of tax on any savings invested, with the Government hoping the planned favourable tax terms will entice savers who currently have around €170 billion on deposit to invest. According to the BPFI survey, almost half of adults (48%) are aware of the scheme, although this drops to 25% of younger adults aged 18-34.

stories.title: Oil set for weekly gain as US ramps up pressure on Iran
stories.summary: Oil prices were steady today and were on track for a second weekly gain in a row after the US threatened to impose the toughest sanctions in history with no end in sight for disruptions to Middle East oil flows. Brent crude futures rose 20 cents, or 0.21%, to $93.98 a barrel this afternoon, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up seven cents, or 0.08%, at $86.90. The Brent benchmark has gained more than 6.1% while WTI has risen 5.3% this week, with both touching their highest since July 24 in the previous session. "The US is taking a very firm stance against Iran, with the blockade back in place and threats of tougher sanctions on Iranian oil exports, and that's why we are seeing oil prices back above $90 a barrel," said ANZ analyst Soni Kumari.

stories.title: Twardek goal helps Galway spoil Dundalk's centenary night
stories.summary: On the night that Dundalk celebrated their centenary of joining the League of Ireland, Galway Utd spoiled the party at Oriel Park as goals in either half from Ed McCarthy and Kris Twardek secured a huge victory for the Tribesmen. Trevor Clarke did pull a late goal back for the Co. Louth side to set up a nervy finish but the 2-1 defeat meant it was a repeat result of the club's first ever game at this level when they lost to Fordsons. With many events around the match, including a special edition jersey being released, John Caulfield’s side turned party poopers as they clinched just their third away win of the campaign. While Ciarán Kilduff’s side dominated proceedings, they didn’t do enough in front of goal as their run without a win now stretches to seven matches, with just two points out of the last 21 on offer.

stories.title: Croke Park keen to host annual Premier League friendlies
stories.summary: Croke Park chiefs are keen to make Premier League pre-season friendlies like Wednesday night's clash between Manchester United and Leeds regular events. The match between the long-standing rivals was the first game of soccer to be played at the home of the GAA since 2009, but was seen as a huge success as a sell-out crowd of 75,000 watched Manchester United beat their old rivals on penalties. The only previous times soccer had been played at the venue were between 2007 and 2009 when it served as the temporary home of the Republic of Ireland during the redevelopment of Lansdowne Road. But Peter McKenna, Croke Park’s stadium and commercial director, is keen to change that to find new revenue streams to put into the GAA.
